description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
The second release candidate for 6.0: faster searches with typos, why each record is in the
      list, and two fixes for words and synonyms in fields with text rules. Nothing here breaks a build.
      
      ### Added
      
      - **Why each record is in the list.** `ScoreEntry16.Source` (`RecordSource`): `Counted`, or shown below
        without being counted: `Fill` (a typo level past the one counted), `MostWords` and `Rest`. Read it
        rather than taking the first `Count` records for the counted ones.
      - **The heaviest field first** (`Ranking.HeaviestFieldFirst`, off by default). Used with
        `Candidates.FillReach`, a record that has every word in its heaviest field, usually the title, comes
        before records that have the words spelt exactly but spread over other fields, even when the title
        has a typo. The list holds the same records and the count is the same, but a record shown without
        being counted can now stand above one that is counted.
      - **The match report names a synonym and its field.** A query word met through a synonym now has
        `Field` and `Fields`, where they were empty, and `QueryWordMatch.Synonym`, the synonym as your
        list writes it ("movie" for "film"). `MatchesByField` counts those words. A word the record holds
        as typed says nothing of the synonym. Field and synonym are still empty where the report finds the
        synonym in no field, or only spread over fields with different text rules.
      
      ### Faster
      
      - **Searches with typos**: finding the words within one, two or three edits of what was typed is
        five to seven times faster.
      - **Searches no record answers in full**, which list the records holding the most of the words, read
        less of the index, and count in an array where common words hold very many records. The slowest of
        them can take half the time or much less. The results are the same.
      - **Word lookups allocate about half as much**, so searches with several words, and many searches at
        once, are faster: 40 % more searches a second on four threads in our test on a product catalogue.
      - **Common words that match very many records**: finding the records and choosing the best of them is
        faster, up to a third off the slowest searches on a large catalogue of short titles.
      
      ### Fixed
      
      - **A word a field's own text rule joins is found as typed.** A field whose rule deletes a separator
        without `KeepOriginal` holds "tv-spill" as one word, "tvspill"; typed with the hyphen, or reached through
        a synonym, it did not find a record holding it in that field only. Now it does, whichever way it is
        written.
      - **A synonym written with a capital letter is found.** A list that gave "Movie" for "film" found
        nothing more for "film"; write synonyms as you like. Searches with such a list find more records.
title: IndxSearchLib
